reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: src/forwback.rs keeps stack scroll counters/positions and mutates shared navigation/display state. overlay_header borrows line rendering and position services rather than acquiring an independent rendered byte owner.
owner_creation.invariant: Scroll positions are values, not ownership of the rendered line.
limitations: The actual byte/attribute owners remain in the line module.

aliases_escapes.analysis: src/forwback.rs obtains each header position from navigation, renders through forw_line/forw_line_pfx and consumes the shared line with put_line. The rendered content must survive that call sequence.
aliases_escapes.invariant: A rendered-line borrow must match the current position and header geometry.
limitations: No generation token binds the temporary position to line-buffer content.

callback_targets.analysis: src/forwback.rs calls line generation, attribute selection, output and repaint directly; no function pointer or heap callback context is retained by overlay_header or the scroll completion path.
callback_targets.invariant: Named rendering calls must preserve their caller-visible owner contract.
limitations: Direct dispatch does not prevent another callee from changing shared display state.

invalidation.analysis: src/forwback.rs can clear navigation positions before repaint and repeatedly replace the current rendered line while scrolling. Existing copied coordinates need revalidation when that shared state changes.
invalidation.invariant: Logical screen invalidation must precede reusing old coordinates.
limitations: This file does not own or release the position-table allocation itself.

mutation_commit.analysis: src/forwback.rs publishes forward positions after rendering and updates first_time/current-line state separately; EOF and repaint decisions depend on the same mutable screen/input snapshot.
mutation_commit.invariant: Position publication must agree with the content actually displayed.
limitations: These are incremental display updates, not an all-or-nothing frame transaction.

release_pair.analysis: src/forwback.rs acquires no local heap block in the header/scroll paths; it borrows rendered line and position owners and must not free their storage. Ending stack counters releases no native resource.
release_pair.invariant: The consuming display layer must not become a second allocator owner.
limitations: This local no-free observation does not prove global rendering owners are balanced.

error_cleanup.analysis: src/forwback.rs backward scanning checks a -1 line result and signal flags to decide whether to stop or continue. It has no local typed distinction proving every lower-layer read/error was diagnosed.
error_cleanup.invariant: An input sentinel and an owner-release obligation must not be conflated.
limitations: No new compatibility or permanent-I/O-failure campaign ran for these branches.

signals_handoff.analysis: src/forwback.rs polls sigs before forward/backward work, yet retains shared display and navigation assumptions across many direct calls. M0-MEM-001 remains open for that coordination.
signals_handoff.invariant: Signal polling is not an exclusive owner-handoff mechanism.
limitations: No specific handler-induced line replacement is claimed from polling alone.
